transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:30 - 16:12 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, Borealis), Arjun Patel (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Product)

Summary: short discovery for PLG/self-serve quickstart + evaluate hosted vs dedicated for initial pilot. customer interested in time-to-first-token and security for PII workloads.

Topics: quickstart credits, api keys, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/dedicated needs, SOC2/KMS, rollout plan

Transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on this account. Diego (SE) is with me. how's every one doing?
00:12 Maya Chen: Doing good, thanks. we're eager to see how fast we can get something live. our timeline is kinda tight, want to show eng leadership a prototype in two weeks.
00:25 Diego Ruiz: great, that's in scope for our PLG quickstart. typical path is self-serve sign up, free credits, then time-to-first-token in minutes. we can also run a dedicated pilot if volume and isolation required.
00:40 Arjun Patel: quick q first - our main concern is latency; customer facing chat with sub-200ms target for short replies. also cost matters, we don't want 10x infra spend.
00:52 Diego Ruiz: yeah, good callout. for sub-200ms depends on model choice and sequence length; Redwood has curated model profiles and we can suggest quantized variants for cost. also smart batching and KV prefix cache can bring token cost down without impacting p50 latency too much.
01:20 Maya Chen: sorry, KV cache?
01:22 Diego Ruiz: key-value cache, kv caching - it stores prefix activations so repeated context doesn't recompute. helps for chat with reused system prompts.
01:34 Sofia Ruiz: there's some background noise, a bit garbled, soz.
01:40 Lena Park: no worries, we'll capture the notes. can you walk us through your stack and data residency needs?
01:48 Maya Chen: sure. infra - GCP us-central1, internal services in k8s, user data is PII, we need audit trails and KMS, and SOC 2 type II is a hard requirement. also some clients want EU residency later.
02:05 Diego Ruiz: ok that maps to Redwood Private or Dedicated depending on whether you want to manage VPC. Hosted can be configured with customer-managed KMS and audit logs, but if you need VPC peering and full control we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.
02:25 Arjun Patel: how different is dedic at the start? we don't have ops capacity for long setup.
02:33 Lena Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity with SLA and dedicated GPU pools. onboarding is typically a couple weeks for provisioning; for fast prototype, the hosted PLG quickstart is faster since it's self-serve. you can spin up API keys and run workloads within minutes. we give free credits to test.
02:50 Maya Chen: perfect. what's included in quickstart? do you provide example prompts, SDKs?
02:57 Diego Ruiz: yep. GitHub quickstart repo, node/python SDK, example prompts and a simple dockerized client to simulate traffic. we'll also share a benchmark sheet to capture your payloads so we can suggest model/quantization profiles.
03:12 Arjun Patel: for security, will hosted keep logs? and can logs be turned off or configured?
03:20 Lena Park: hosted retains logs for telemetry; we can enable minimal retention and provide audit logs. for full control you can go Dedicated/Private with customer-managed KMS and no long-term retention. we also support SAML SSO and RBAC for org teams.
03:40 Sofia Ruiz: any customers doing EU region + SOC2?
03:45 Diego Ruiz: yes, a couple enterprise customers use our EU region with SOC2 controls; we can share redacted attestation and architecture docs. i'll put those in follow-up.
04:02 Maya Chen: competition - we're already evaluating OpenAI and Anthropic, and our infra team is looking at running models on SageMaker. why Redwood vs them for quickstart?
04:18 Lena Park: two main things: developer experience for real production inference and predictable economics. hosted is fastest to validate; Dedicated and Private paths are there when you need data isolation or SLAs. We also publish model performance profiles so you don't guess at latency/cost.
04:36 Arjun Patel: question on pricing - is it per-token like others?
04:39 Lena Park: hosted is usage-based, per-token/embedding; Dedicated is reserved capacity + lower unit costs. we can run a cost projection once we get sample query volume.
04:52 Diego Ruiz: and for quick experiments we give free credits so your team can run the end-to-end flow and measure time-to-first-token. typically teams get API key, run a small demo app, and in <30 minutes they see first responses.
05:10 Maya Chen: sounds good. would like to run a small benchmark with 5k qps bursts?
05:17 Diego Ruiz: 5k qps bursts are high; for that scale Dedicated is more predictable but we can simulate with hosted to give guidance. can you share typical payload sizes and expected concurrency?
05:30 Arjun Patel: payloads are 300-800 tokens avg, concurrency expect 200-500 concurrent users initially.
05:38 Diego Ruiz: ok that'll inform batching windows; bigger payloads change memory footprint and latency. we'll run a baseline with similar sample and get back with tradeoffs.
05:50 Maya Chen: about compliance - for Hosted with KMS, is key material stored in Redwood or in our KMS?
05:58 Lena Park: we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) so KMS can be in your cloud. cryptographic operations remain customer-controlled.
06:08 Sofia Ruiz: what's the usual POC timeline? two weeks prototype then pilot?
06:12 Lena Park: typical path: quickstart (days), prototype/demo (1-2 weeks), pilot (4-8 weeks) for production readiness. we'll align to your timeline.
06:22 Arjun Patel: any friction in getting API keys? we want an automated flow tied to our org user provisioning.
06:28 Lena Park: self-serve sign-up is standard; for enterprise we can provision via SSO and invite users. we'll include steps.
06:35 Maya Chen: ok, what do you need from us to start the quickstart?
06:40 Lena Park: ideally - a sample of your payloads, an expected QPS/concurrency number, and a primary contact for setup. we'll issue a quickstart org, credits, and guide.
06:51 Maya Chen: i'll send that.
06:53 Diego Ruiz: quick note on model selection - for low-latency chat we often recommend smaller quantized models or 1.3-2.7B variants depending on quality tradeoffs. we can show sample latency numbers in the benchmark.
07:05 Arjun Patel: do you support streaming and tool calling? we need streaming for progressive render in chat.
07:10 Diego Ruiz: yes streaming responses supported, and function/tool calling patterns work with our SDKs. caveat: streaming affects token accounting slightly.
07:20 Sofia Ruiz: are there any gotchas with our k8s setup? we'd like to host on-prem later possibly.
07:26 Diego Ruiz: for on-prem/private, we provide a package and control plane; air-gapped deployment takes more time but is possible. we'll share a checklist for network and storage requirements.
07:39 Maya Chen: ok good. next steps?
07:42 Lena Park: recap - Lena will send quickstart guide, free credits, security docs; Diego will run a latency/cost baseline after you share sample payloads; Maya to share volumes and compliance reqs. schedule deep-dive next week for technicals.
07:58 Maya Chen: sounds great, thanks.
08:00 Lena Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up. bye.

Notes on transcription: some words may be slightly off; speakers occasionally overlap. references: quickstart github link (sent post-call), SOC2 attestation (link), benchmark spreadsheet (template).
